deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. The page is the back of a letter cover addressed 'Sr. Hochwohlgeboren Herrn Hofrath und Ritter Gauss, Director der Sternwarte in Göttingen', marked 'frei', with a postmark '2 AUG'. Gauss used it as scratch paper. The neighbouring pages concern the cubic transformation of the arithmetic-geometric mean and theta functions. The previous page has the 'Dreitheilung' modular relations p^4=a^3c, etc. The next page has t = M(1,kk)/M(1+kk,1-kk), log(1/x) = a t, and the quotient (1-2x+2x^4-2x^9)/(1+2x+2x^4+2x^9). This page studies how a purely imaginary modulus Mi (equivalently a theta-nome argument) transforms under an integral unimodular substitution.

(1) General transformation. Gauss sets N = (alpha*M - beta*i)/(delta + gamma*M*i) with alpha*delta - beta*gamma = 1. Since alpha*M - beta*i = -i(alpha*Mi + beta), we get N*i = (alpha*tau + beta)/(gamma*tau + delta) with tau = Mi (my rewriting). So N*i is the image of tau = Mi under the SL(2,Z) Moebius map.

Multiplying by the conjugate (delta - gamma*M*i), the real part of the numerator is (alpha*delta - beta*gamma)M = M. Gauss's result is
N = [M - (beta*delta + alpha*gamma*M^2) i] / (delta^2 + gamma^2 M^2).
Equivalently Im(tau') = M/(delta^2+gamma^2 M^2) and Re(tau') = (beta*delta+alpha*gamma*M^2)/(delta^2+gamma^2 M^2).

He writes this as N = (1 + f i)/g, i.e. g = (delta^2+gamma^2 M^2)/M and f = -(beta*delta+alpha*gamma*M^2)/M. He then derives the linear system
delta*f + beta*g = -gamma*M,
gamma*f + alpha*g = delta/M.
Both follow from alpha*delta - beta*gamma = 1 (verified below). Solving it for f (begun with 'f =') would recover the substitution from the reduced value.

The special case M = 1 is noted: N = [1 - (alpha*gamma+beta*delta) i]/(gamma^2+delta^2). This is the expression on the left with x in place of alpha.

(2) Variant normalisation. He also writes N = (alpha - beta*i)/(delta + gamma*i) with alpha*delta - beta*gamma = M, and Ni = (alpha*M + beta*i)/(gamma*M + delta*i). These look like trial normalisations; the second identity does not follow literally from the first (see errors).

(3) Composition of substitutions. He composes a second substitution with a first, e.g. [p(alpha M - beta i) + 3q(...)] / [r(beta + alpha M i) + 3s(...)]. For the example 3M - 2i over 7(..)+10Mi, i.e. the matrix [[3,2],[10,7]] of determinant 1, he forms
[alpha(3M-2i) + 3beta(10M-7i)] / [3delta(7+10Mi) + gamma(2+3M)].
He then imposes a vanishing coefficient, alpha*r + 3*gamma*s = 0, giving r = -3gamma, s = alpha (or r = -gamma, s = alpha/3).
The resulting choices are alpha=7, beta=-2, delta=3, gamma=-10. Then alpha*delta - beta*gamma = 21 - 20 = 1, and this matrix is exactly the inverse of [[3,2],[10,7]]. The products 61-42 = ... and -60+42 are entries of such matrix products.
A second unimodular set, alpha=21, beta=-2, delta=1, gamma=-10, also has determinant 21 - 20 = 1.

(4) Numerical example of reduction. (13M + 2i)/(58M + 9i) = Ni has matrix [[13,2],[58,9]] with determinant 117 - 116 = 1. The Euclidean scheme beside it is: 58,13,6,1 with quotients 4,2,6 (58 = 4*13+6, 13 = 2*6+1), and 9,2,1 with 9 = 4*2+1. This is the continued-fraction decomposition of the substitution into elementary steps. It is exactly how an SL(2,Z) matrix is factored into translations and inversions when reducing a point (or a binary quadratic form).

(5) Gaussian-integer side computations.
- (1+3i)/(2-i) = (-1+7i)/5.
- (1-2i)/(1+2i) = (-3-4i)/5.
- (1+2i)(1+4i) = -7+6i.
- 7+6i is the conjugate of 7-6i; the norms 65 = |1+8i|^2 and 85 = |7-6i|^2 are noted.
- (1+8i)/(7-6i) = (-41+62i)/85, written as (-41+6?i)/85.
These are checks of quotients of Gaussian integers, i.e. of the transformation formula for particular complex values. The small drawings (house/church, crosses) are doodles.
errors: Ni = (alpha M - beta i)/(-gamma M + delta i): from N = (alpha M - beta i)/(delta + gamma M i) one gets N i = (alpha M - beta i)/(gamma M - delta i). Gauss's expression is -N i, so there is a sign slip, or N is implicitly redefined.

In the variant N = (alpha - beta i)/(delta + gamma i) with alpha delta - beta gamma = M, the stated Ni = (alpha M + beta i)/(gamma M + delta i) does not follow literally; it is a different (exploratory) normalisation.

The numerator term 3q(gamma M - delta M) is probably meant as 3q(gamma M - delta M i) or similar. The denominator is overwritten and the composition formula is only partially legible; it is not a completed derivation.
No errors in the main identity N = (M-(beta delta+alpha gamma M^2)i)/(delta^2+gamma^2M^2), the linear relations for f and g, the determinant checks, or the Gaussian-integer quotients.

results.what: Image of tau = Mi under tau -> (alpha tau+beta)/(gamma tau+delta), alpha delta - beta gamma = 1: Im = M/(delta^2+gamma^2M^2), Re = (beta delta+alpha gamma M^2)/(delta^2+gamma^2M^2)
results.modern_name: action of the modular group SL(2,Z) on the upper half-plane; imaginary-part formula Im(g tau) = Im tau/|c tau+d|^2

results.what: Factoring a unimodular substitution (13,2;58,9) via the Euclidean algorithm / continued fraction to reduce a point
results.modern_name: reduction to the fundamental domain; generation of SL(2,Z) by S and T
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones, reduction of forms); Klein/Dedekind for the geometric picture

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's use of the modular group acting on the modulus/theta argument, with reduction to a fundamental region, is known from his Nachlass (Werke III/VIII, the fundamental-domain figure) and from historical studies (Fricke, Schlesinger, Gray). The page is routine working computation within that known programme, tied to his AGM and theta studies.

transcription_corrections: Address line: 'Ds Professorhonde[?]' should read 'Sr. Hochwohlgeboren' (standard address formula).
'(-41+6i)/85' is most likely '(-41+62i)/85', the value of (1+8i)/(7-6i).
The crossed-out denominator '[-7M-] + 10Mi' appears as a correction to '7 + 10Mi' (matrix [[3,2],[10,7]]), consistent with the later '3delta(7+10Mi)'.
'1-2i over 1+2i' is a fraction, and '1+4i' (with '2+3i') belongs to the product (1+2i)(1+4i) = -7+6i.
The left expression '(x - beta i)/(delta+gamma i)' is likely '(alpha - beta i)/(delta+gamma i)' (or a deliberate variable), the M=1 case.
